merger_description:
Movac Fund, as trustee for Movac Growth Fund 7 Limited Partnership (**Movac GF7 LP**) proposes to purchase Series C Preference Shares and Ordinary Shares in Advanced Navigation Pty. Ltd (**AdNav**), as set out in the draft transaction documents provided in the application (the **Acquisition**).

The Acquisition is part of the second close of AdNav's Series C funding raise, and Movac Fund proposes to acquire a combination of Ordinary Shares and Series C Preference Shares in exchange for cash payments. Once the Acquisition is completed, Movac will have a small total aggregate shareholding in AdNav.

Movac Fund is a venture capital fund vehicle managed by Movac Growth Limited (**Movac Growth**), which is associated with Movac Limited (**Movac**). Movac is a venture capital firm based in New Zealand that through its funds primarily invests in New Zealand or New Zealand-connected early- and growth-stage technology companies. Movac has a focus on investments in the Software-as-a-service (**SaaS**) and deep tech sectors. It also holds investments in several Australian and North American portfolio companies.

AdNav develops AI-powered robotic and navigation technologies for defence, land, air, sea and space applications. It combines AI, software and sensor technology to provide positioning services where GPS is unavailable. AdNav primarily supplies inertial navigation systems, acoustic navigation systems, and underwater robotics/vehicles. Its products are usually sub-components and are primarily supplied to systems integrators rather than end users/consumers.

determination_table_content.details:
Movac Growth Fund 7 Custodial Limited as trustee for Movac
Growth Fund 7 Limited Partnership (Movac Fund) applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of a small
shareholding in Advanced Navigation Pty. Ltd. (Advanced
Navigation), as described in the transaction documents provided as
part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Movac Fund, is managed by Movac Growth Limited,
which is associated with Movac Limited (Movac). Movac is a venture
capital firm based in New Zealand that through its funds primarily
invests in New Zealand or New Zealand-connected early-and growth-
stage technology companies. Movac has a focus on investments in
the Software-as-a-Service and deep tech sectors. It also holds
investments in several Australian and North American portfolio
companies.
The target, Advanced Navigation, develops AI-powered robotic and
navigation technologies for defence, land, air, sea and space
applications. It combines AI, software and sensor technology to
provide positioning services where GPS is unavailable. Advanced
Navigation primarily supplies inertial navigation systems, acoustic
navigation systems, and underwater robotics/vehicles. Its products
are usually sub-components and are primarily supplied to systems
integrators rather than end users/consumers.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver and had regard
to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the size of the interest in AdNav being acquired by Movac is
expected to be small
b. there is no horizontal or vertical overlap between Movac and
Advanced Navigation in the supply of AI-powered
navigational systems.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
